evidence: deepseek: "Try all triples in lexicographic order"; qwen: "Build adjacency list using sets"; glm: "Find common neighbors w"
affordance_in_statement: Specifically, you need to find three distinct processes such that each process in the group has a mutual exclusion constraint with both of the other two processes in the group.
removal_suggestion: Do not explicitly identify the target as three mutually adjacent processes. Describe it indirectly as the lexicographically smallest triple for which every assignment to two processors violates at least one listed exclusion, requiring contestants to derive the triangle condition from the scheduling scenario.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Directly models exclusions as an adjacency matrix and scans triples in lexicographic order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: each process in the group has a mutual exclusion constraint with both of the other two processes

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds adjacency sets and searches common neighbors to detect a triangle.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Sorts edges and searches their common neighbors, using the explicit triangle structure and ordering rule.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The identifiers must be printed in ascending order ... output the one that is lexicographically smallest.

common_affordance: The statement explicitly reduces the scheduling problem to finding a triangle in an undirected conflict graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its bitset-based search did not correctly enforce the required ascending third vertex and/or lexicographic ordering when selecting a common neighbor, so it can report a valid but non-minimal or improperly ordered triple.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit pairwise-mutual-exclusion characterization with an indirect two-processor infeasibility condition: ask for the lexicographically smallest triple for which no assignment of the three processes to the two processors satisfies all listed exclusions. Keep the input and output unchanged, but make deriving the triangle characterization necessary.
regression_risk: This may make the already-defeated gpt-oss-120b appear correct on cases where its output happens to be ordered, although its selection logic remains unreliable.
